clue.text: Extreme example of all responsible for one

definitions.meaning: the idiom 'the mother of all' or its fuller form names the biggest, most extreme instance of something
a pair of parents are responsible for a child, the 'one' here

explanation.surface: Someone is described as the ultimate case of a group that answers for a single person.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiomatic phrase means the supreme instance of something, and literally names the two parents who brought one into being.

clue.text: Offer me a red form to provide a sense of security

indicators.note: the letters are made to provide something new, a loose Araucaria-style signal that they are rearranged

parts.note: the fodder, used letter for letter

explanation.surface: Someone asks to be handed a red document that will reassure them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'form' looks like the anagram signal but its letters are needed; the rearranging is signalled by 'to provide'. This is one of Roosevelt's Four Freedoms.
explanation.definitionFit: Being free of fright is a state of safety and calm, which is what a feeling of security is.

clue.text: Hired in the tandoori, say

parts.note: the tandoori, an Indian dish, hints that the word wanted is the Anglo-Indian term for hired, as used of a hired carriage

explanation.surface: A cook has been taken on for a spell at an Indian restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: The tandoori is not a restaurant but a pointer to India: the answer is an Anglo-Indian word for hired, used of hired carriages and servants.
explanation.definitionFit: In Anglo-Indian usage this word describes something taken on hire, such as a hackney carriage.

clue.text: Animal doing some work in English tree

indicators.note: the shortened word goes inside the tree

parts.note: the elm is a tree

indicators.note: only part of the following word is used, its last letter dropped

explanation.surface: A creature is busy toiling inside an English tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doing' is only a link; 'some' signals that the word after it is cut short before going into the tree.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a nematode, a tiny worm-like creature that infests plants, so it is broadly an animal.

clue.text: Instrument for a pound a point

parts.note: L stands for a pound sterling, from Latin libra
a thorn is a sharp point on a plant

explanation.surface: Someone is selling a musical instrument at a bargain price per point.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a brass instrument of the saxhorn family, pitched in E flat.

clue.text: Very bad politician and model must be separated

definitions.note: the answer is an old word for to separate, used here in its participial, adjectival sense

parts.note: dire means dreadful, very bad
MP, Member of Parliament
the Model T Ford gives T for model

explanation.surface: An awful MP and a fashion model have to be kept apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Model' is the Model T Ford, so just T.
explanation.definitionFit: This rare word, from Latin diremptus, means torn apart or forcibly divided.

clue.text: Beheaded prophet (beheaded, dead) going in advance

indicators.note: the prophet loses his head, his first letter

parts.note: Jonah is the Old Testament prophet swallowed by a whale

indicators.note: dead loses its first letter too

explanation.surface: A prophet who has been decapitated and killed goes on before others.
explanation.walkthrough: Both words lose their first letters: ONAH from JONAH and EAD from DEAD.
explanation.definitionFit: To go on ahead is to travel in advance of the rest of a party.

clue.text: Uncertainty teaches information

annotationWithheld.why: Uncertainty teaches information (9): the parse is TEACHES + IN rearranged, with 'information' read as 'in formation', one word giving both the IN and the anagram signal

clue.text: Book about principal, not a strong head maybe, yet beginning

parts.note: re means concerning, about
main means chief, principal
soft is the opposite of strong

indicators.note: maybe suggests the letters of the word head could be arranged otherwise
only the first letter of yet is taken

explanation.surface: A book about a headteacher who is weak-minded yet just starting out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not a strong head' looks like SOFTHEAD, but only SOFT comes from 'not a strong'; HEAD is rearranged by 'maybe' to HEDA, and 'beginning' gives Y from 'yet'.
explanation.definitionFit: This is Kazuo Ishiguro's Booker-winning novel about an English butler.

clue.text: It's maybe left to staircase when it's not there

definitions.text: It's maybe left to staircase when it's not there

indicators.note: maybe signals the pooled letters can be rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
the letters I, T, S are the ones that are not there

explanation.surface: When a staircase is missing, perhaps the moving kind is left to do the job.
explanation.walkthrough: Put L and TO with STAIRCASE, take out the letters of IT'S ('when it's not there') and rearrange what is left. The whole clue also describes the answer: a moving staircase.
explanation.definitionFit: A moving staircase is exactly this, so the whole clue describes the thing as well as building it.

clue.text: Confession of folly could produce tea

definitions.meaning: split as two words it is a terse 'I am an ass', admitting to being a fool
a black tea from north-east India

explanation.surface: Owning up to foolishness might lead to a cup of tea.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer into ASS AM, an inverted 'am an ass', to see the confession.
explanation.definitionFit: This Indian region gives its name to a strong black tea.

clue.text: Game boy detailed to enter how we used to reach the operator

indicators.note: the shortened word goes into the phone instruction

parts.words: how we used to reach the operator
parts.note: on old British phones you dialled 0 to get the operator

indicators.note: de-tailed, losing its last letter

parts.note: taken as written, then shortened

explanation.surface: A lad is sent off to get into an old-fashioned telephone routine.
explanation.walkthrough: Older British phones reached the operator by dialling zero, written as the letter O; 'detailed' means losing a tail.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a juggling game with a spool spun on a string between two sticks.

clue.text: The West's triumph begins with experts

parts.note: Mae West, the film star, gives MAE'S

indicators.note: only the start of the word triumph is used, the rest dropped

explanation.surface: The victory of the West opens with specialists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The West' suggests the Western world but it is Mae West; TRI is the beginning of 'triumph'.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the plural of the Italian word for a master, especially an eminent musician or conductor.

clue.text: See 16
Setter with soul of butcher?

parts.note: in crosswords the setter refers to themself as me
atman is the Hindu term for the soul or self

explanation.surface: A dog breed with the spirit of a meat-cutter?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setter' looks like the dog, but it is the crossword compiler, so ME.
explanation.definitionFit: This hyphenated word is an old term for someone who sells meat, which is what a butcher does.

clue.text: Slowish with opposite number

parts.note: and means together with
anti means against, opposed

explanation.surface: Something goes slowly with a different figure.
explanation.definitionFit: This musical direction means a little faster than andante, so a moderately slow tempo.

clue.text: Second sight?

parts.note: a second view of a moment in sport, shown again on television, not the psychic gift

explanation.surface: Someone asks about the gift of clairvoyance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second sight' usually means clairvoyance; here it is a literal second look at a piece of play.
explanation.definitionFit: A rerun of a moment of play on television gives viewers a second look at it.

clue.text: Information touches outside row

indicators.note: the touching word goes round the noise

parts.note: tig is a touch, as in the children's chasing game
a din is a noisy row

explanation.surface: News reaches people outside a dispute.
explanation.walkthrough: Tig is the British playground chasing game, where tagging someone is to 'tig' them.
explanation.definitionFit: Tidings are news, and news is information passed on.

clue.text: See 16
A penny for a shilling in the dish at a masque

indicators.note: a penny stands in place of a shilling

parts.note: risotto is an Italian rice dish

explanation.surface: Someone swaps a penny for a shilling when buying the main course at a costume ball.
explanation.walkthrough: In old British money D was the abbreviation for a penny and S for a shilling; replace the S in RISOTTO with D.
explanation.definitionFit: A ridotto was an eighteenth-century public entertainment with music and dancing, often masked, much like a masque.

clue.text: He-otter in trouble, at that

indicators.note: the letters of the male otter are disturbed and rearranged

explanation.surface: A male otter is in difficulties, and that is that.
explanation.definitionFit: This formal word means to that thing or in addition to that, matching the phrase given.

clue.text: Take round some fluid from the body to lead us to heaven?

parts.note: O is round in shape

indicators.note: only part of the body fluid word is used, its last letter dropped

parts.note: lymph is a clear bodily fluid
taken as written

explanation.surface: Take a sample of a bodily fluid to help us get to paradise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take' and 'to lead' are link words; 'some' signals the fluid's word is cut short.
explanation.definitionFit: The mountain home of the Greek gods serves as their heaven, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Feels no grief for nobody else

indicators.note: coming to grief, the letters are wrecked and reassembled

explanation.surface: Someone untouched by sorrow cares about no one but themself.
explanation.definitionFit: The reflexive pronoun refers to oneself alone, so to no other person.

clue.text: Food for holy person in former assizes

indicators.note: the saint goes inside the old courts

parts.note: oyer, short for oyer and terminer, was a former English court session like the assizes
St is the abbreviation for saint

explanation.surface: Something to eat for a saint at a court of the past.
explanation.walkthrough: Oyer and terminer was an old English commission to hear criminal cases, held at the assizes.
explanation.definitionFit: These shellfish are eaten as a delicacy, so they are a kind of food.

clue.text: Queen on river which makes one sneeze

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina
the Rhine is a major European river

explanation.surface: The monarch on a river trip finds something that sets off a sneeze.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' means the first piece sits above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: An errhine is a substance snuffed up the nose to cause sneezing or a nasal discharge.

clue.text: See 16
The religious right confined by primate

indicators.note: the R is held inside the primate

parts.note: a monkey is a primate

explanation.surface: A clergyman is trapped by an ape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'primate' suggests an archbishop, but it is the animal; 'The religious' means monks collectively.
explanation.definitionFit: This word means monks as a body, or monastic life, which is the religious in the sense of members of orders.

clue.text: Not enough damage to be a handicap?

definitions.meaning: a slight graze or mark, too small to count as real harm
in golf and racing, the zero handicap of a player who gets no allowance

explanation.surface: Is too little harm enough to count as a disadvantage?
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a superficial mark and the term for a zero handicap in sport.

clue.text: Beat — from time to time, died

parts.note: hr, hour, is a unit of time
hr, hour, is a unit of time
ob, from Latin obiit, means died

explanation.surface: A pulse stopped every so often, then the patient died.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from time to time' looks like a signal for alternate letters, but it gives two pieces: T for 'time' and HR (hour) for the second 'time'.
explanation.definitionFit: A throb is a single pulse or beat, as of the heart.

clue.text: Send away footballer who won't start without his team

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, round the team
the footballer's name loses its first letter

parts.note: Pele, the great Brazilian footballer
a football team is an eleven, XI in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Banish a player who refuses to start without his side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside; a football side has eleven players, the Roman numeral XI.
explanation.definitionFit: To exile someone is to banish them from their country, to send them away.

clue.text: Was first performed when empire changed colour

indicators.note: the letters of empire are changed into a new order

parts.note: red is a colour

explanation.surface: The empire turned a different colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A play or film premiered when it had its first public performance.

clue.text: Act may be read here — clue to messy lab.

definitions.meaning: the Riot Act was read out to order an unruly crowd to disperse
lab is short for the Labour Party, and a disorderly party gathering would be described this way

explanation.surface: A legal act can be read out at a chaotic laboratory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lab.' looks like a laboratory but, with its full stop, is the Labour Party; a rowdy Labour conference fits the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the legal term for a disorderly gathering, the kind where the Riot Act would be read.
